report_name: OpenCode Breach Exposes OpenAI, Anthropic API Keys, Leads to Fraud

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The attacker gained initial access by exploiting an unspecified vulnerability in a legacy OpenCode system.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: The core of the attack was the theft of API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google AI services, which function as application access tokens.

attack_patterns.name: Resource Hijacking
attack_patterns.description: Attackers used stolen API keys to consume victims' AI service credits for a 'distillation attack', likely to train their own AI models.

campaigns.name: OpenCode Distillation Attack Campaign
campaigns.description: A campaign where an attacker compromised the OpenCode Console, stole user API keys for major AI providers, and used them in a 'distillation attack' to hijack computational resources.

identities.name: OpenCode
identities.description: An open-source AI coding agent from Anomaly Innovations whose Console product was breached, leading to the exposure of user-stored API keys.

identities.name: Anomaly Innovations
identities.description: The parent company of the compromised OpenCode AI coding agent.

identities.name: OpenAI
identities.description: AI service provider whose user API keys were stolen from OpenCode and used for fraudulent computation.

identities.name: Anthropic
identities.description: AI service provider whose user API keys were stolen from OpenCode and used for fraudulent computation.

identities.name: Google
identities.description: Cloud and AI service provider whose user API keys were stolen from OpenCode and used for fraudulent computation.

identities.name: OpenCode Console Users
identities.description: The group of users (1.4% of the total) whose API keys were exposed in the breach and subsequently used for fraudulent activities, resulting in financial loss.

infrastructure.name: OpenCode Legacy System
infrastructure.description: A legacy system slated for decommissioning that was compromised by an attacker, leading to the exposure of user-stored API keys.
